title: Close caller-owned MCP HTTP clients on every connection exit path
summary: When an MCP connection creates a custom HTTP client for headers, register that caller-owned client on the connection AsyncExitStack so both normal exit and initialization failure close it.

symptoms: A custom-header MCP HTTP connection leaves the caller-owned SDK HTTP client open after normal context exit.
The same client remains open when ClientSession.initialize raises an expected exception.
Five existing connection tests pass while two focused lifecycle regressions fail only at the final closed-state assertion.

applies_when: A wrapper creates and owns a custom async HTTP client before passing it into an SDK transport context.
The wrapper already owns an AsyncExitStack covering normal exit and initialization failure.
A focused regression can observe the real client object while isolating network writes.
exclusions: Abstain when the transport context creates and exclusively owns the HTTP client.
Abstain when registering the callback would cause a shared client to be closed by more than one owner.
Do not treat transport-isolated regression coverage as live-network end-to-end verification.
Do not infer AEG cross-agent transfer or token savings from this local archival record.

failed_attempts.approach: Create a custom SDK HTTP client for headers and pass it to the streamable HTTP transport without registering caller-owned cleanup.
failed_attempts.observed_result: Normal connection exit and expected initialization failure both left the real client open; each SDK environment reported five passing existing tests and two lifecycle failures.
failed_attempts.why_failed: The wrapper created the client but transferred neither ownership nor an aclose callback to its AsyncExitStack.

recovery_steps: Identify which layer creates and therefore owns the custom HTTP client.
Immediately after creation, register http_client.aclose on the connection's existing AsyncExitStack.
Keep the SDK transport context responsible for its own resources while the caller stack closes the injected client.
Verify both normal context exit and the path where ClientSession.initialize raises.
Run the same focused regression against MCP SDK 1.29.1 and 2.1.1 without live network I/O.

verification_method.summary: At tested PR head 8a2d825, two frozen lifecycle regressions failed only because the caller-owned client stayed open under both MCP SDK versions. Registering http_client.aclose on the AsyncExitStack made all seven tests pass in both environments.

agent_ready_instructions: Use this record only when a wrapper creates and owns a custom async HTTP client that is injected into an MCP transport. Confirm ownership first. Register the client's aclose callback on the wrapper's existing AsyncExitStack immediately after creation, then verify normal exit and initialization failure with the real client and isolated network writes. Abstain for shared or transport-owned clients. Deduplicate as anthropics/skills#1742:mcp-http-client-lifecycle:8a2d825fa2d5fbaf2d375554985bd80503e4eda0. Do not infer cross-agent transfer.
